title: Hello Rectangle
description: Start here: what a key-click is and why the keyboard is the tool palette, then draw rectangles two ways (by diagonal, by two edges), change the frame's shape, and read the status and available-keys boxes to keep learning on your own.

bubble.title: Welcome to NibGlider
bubble.body: The mouse steers the cursor, but keys do the clicking. This tour points at the controls you will need.

bubble.title: What is a key-click?
bubble.body: A key-click is a click made with a key instead of the mouse button. You steer the cursor with the mouse, and a key press does the clicking — so the point lands exactly where the cursor sits at the moment of the press, with no mouse-button push nudging it off target. Press Watch demo and watch one key press place a corner.

demo.title: Steering only
demo.body: The cursor is moving, but nothing is placed yet. The mouse only steers.

demo.title: The press is the click
demo.body: Pressing I now. The first corner lands exactly where the cursor is at this moment.

demo.title: The corner stayed put
demo.body: Steering again only stretches the preview. The corner stays exactly where the I press put it.

demo.title: Q cancels
demo.body: Q cancels the half-drawn rectangle. Every drawing here works this way: steer with the mouse, click with a key.

bubble.title: The keyboard is the tool palette
bubble.body: Every tool and action here is a key, and the keys you can use right now are listed in the available-keys box. Your mouse hand steers while your keyboard hand picks tools and clicks, so both hands work at once. Nothing important hides in menus — if it can be done, a key does it.

bubble.title: Watch it draw first
bubble.body: Press Watch demo: the program steers the cursor itself and presses I twice to draw a rectangle, live on the canvas.

demo.title: First corner
demo.body: Steering to the first corner of the diagonal.

demo.title: Second corner
demo.body: The I key starts Rect by Diagonal. Now steering to the opposite corner.

demo.title: Done
demo.body: The second I press deposits the rectangle, exactly as your own key presses would.

bubble.title: Your turn: press I
bubble.body: Steer the mouse where you want the first corner, then press the I key to start Rect by Diagonal — the same key the demo pressed.

bubble.title: Place the opposite corner
bubble.body: Steer to the opposite corner and press I again to deposit your rectangle.

bubble.title: Watch: rectangle by two edges
bubble.body: Press Watch demo: the program steers the cursor itself and presses U twice to draw a rectangle from two edges, live on the canvas.

demo.title: Second edge
demo.body: The U key starts Rect by Two Edges. Now steering to the opposite edge.

demo.title: Done
demo.body: The second U press deposits the rectangle, exactly as your own key presses would.

bubble.title: Your turn: press U
bubble.body: Steer the mouse where you want to start, then press the U key to start Rect by Two Edges — the same key the demo pressed.

bubble.title: Place the second edge
bubble.body: Steer to the second edge and press U again to deposit your rectangle.

bubble.title: Change the frame's shape
bubble.body: This selector in the Rect Keys section chooses the shape the frame draws. Open it and choose the Polygon card under Polygons — the next rectangle you draw will put a polygon inside its frame.

bubble.title: The status box
bubble.body: The status box tells you what is happening and what you can do next.

bubble.title: The available keys box
bubble.body: The available keys box tells you what keys you can use. You can learn how to use many keys on your own from these two boxes.

bubble.title: One tutorial per section
bubble.body: That is the pattern: watch first, then do it yourself. Help ▸ Tutorials has a short tutorial like this one for each section of the panel — paint, text, arranging, pages, and more. Open it whenever you want a guided first run at a section.
